hook.text: Pop's first mix put most of the instruments on one side of the stereo and the vocals on the other.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: September to October 1972, CBS Studios, London

sentences.text: The first two Stooges albums had little commercial success, and the group had split up.
Pop's heroin addiction was getting worse when David Bowie stepped in.
Pop signed with Columbia as a solo artist and moved to London to make an album with guitarist James Williamson.
When they could not find a suitable rhythm section in England, Williamson suggested bringing in Ron and Scott Asheton, both former Stooges.
The band reformed under the name Iggy and the Stooges, and the elder Asheton, its founding guitarist, reluctantly agreed to switch to bass.
Staff engineer Mike Ross-Trevor worked on the recording.
Pop said Columbia insisted on a ballad for each side of the record: "Gimme Danger" and "I Need Somebody".
Because the budget was tight, Bowie reworked seven of the eight songs in one day at Western Sound Recorders in Los Angeles, and Pop kept his own mix of "Search and Destroy".
Bowie later recalled that on some songs only three of the 24 tracks were used, and that he often raised and lowered the vocal.
Columbia dropped the band after roughly a year of touring, and the group split up in February 1974.
While on day release from rehab, Pop recorded Kill City with Williamson.
In 1993 Bomp Records released a selection of the original mixes as Rough Power.
In 1996 Columbia invited Pop to remix the whole record for CD, and the remixed edition came out on 22 April 1997.
In 2012 both mixes were remastered for a double LP released for Record Store Day, and in 2023 they were remastered again for the album's fiftieth anniversary.

listen_for.text: Pop says Bowie ran this guitar through a Time Cube, a bent plastic tube that makes the sound hit you with an echo.

listen_for.track: Your Pretty Face Is Going to Hell
listen_for.text: Pop says Bowie also ran the drums through the Time Cube, wanting the drummer to sound like someone beating a log.
Robert Christgau says the celeste can finally be heard on this track in Pop's remix.
